subject: Art & Design
title: Licensing: Why Free Fonts Aren't Always Free
description: A fast breakdown of Licensing: Why Free Fonts Aren't Always Free for builders.

hook.text: A startup used a 'free' font on their product. Then they got a $20,000 licensing invoice.

buildup.text: Fonts have licenses. Free for personal use often means paid for commercial use.

discovery.text: Google Fonts are truly free (open source). Many others require per-seat or per-pageview licenses.

twist.text: Embedding a licensed font in a mobile app can cost thousands — separate from the web license.

climax.text: Always check the license before shipping. 'I downloaded it' is not a legal defense.

punchline.text: The font is free until the lawyer says otherwise.

quiz.question: What does 'free for personal use' mean for fonts?
options: Commercial use (products, websites) may require a paid license
You can use it anywhere without restrictions
It only works on free software

details.summary: Font licensing determines how typefaces can be used — desktop, web, app, e-book, and broadcast often require separate licenses at different price tiers. 'Free' fonts may restrict commercial use, modification, or redistribution. Ignoring licensing risks legal action and financial penalties.
details.whyItMatters: Font licensing is one of the most misunderstood areas of design. Using a font without proper licensing is copyright infringement, and foundries actively enforce their rights. Understanding licensing prevents costly legal issues.
takeaways: Different uses (desktop, web, app) often need separate licenses
Free fonts may restrict commercial use or modification
Unlicensed font use is copyright infringement with real penalties

faq.question: Can you use any font in a logo?
faq.answer: Only if the license permits it. Many font licenses allow use in static graphics (including logos) but not in editable formats. Some restrict use in trademarks entirely. Always check the specific license. Converting text to outlines for a logo is usually permitted but should be verified.

faq.question: What is the SIL Open Font License?
faq.answer: The SIL OFL is the most common open-source font license. It allows free use, modification, and redistribution, including commercial use. The main restriction: modified versions can't be sold by themselves and must use a different name. Google Fonts and many open-source fonts use this license.
